summary: Full backend + frontend E2E for Scheduler & Calendar Management app. Backend: 21/21 pytest tests pass (auth, RBAC, events, availability, preferences, notifications dispatch, voice parse/schedule/simulate-call, admin ops). Frontend: All 3 role logins work with correct role-specific dashboards. Calendar event create + pill display works. Preferences persist across reload (phone, reminder, toggles). Voice parse produces correct title/duration/attendee, confirm-schedule creates event, simulate-call renders 5-step Twilio log and creates event. RBAC blocks USER from /api/admin/users (403 verified via frontend fetch). Google Calendar card shows 'Not connected' state.
critical_code_review_comments: Preferences PUT relies on stale state closure (onBlur uses `prefs` snapshot at render time) — works because setPrefs updates before blur fires in practice, but could race. Consider passing next-value directly.
Voice `supportsSpeech` uses SSR-unsafe access (guarded with typeof window OK). Fine.

Backend availability endpoint uses string comparison on ISO date; timezone-naive ISO storage is consistent so it works, but events stored via voice may have different offsets from dateparser — currently unused since RETURN_AS_TIMEZONE_AWARE=False.
React hydration warning `<span> cannot be a child of <option>` comes from Emergent visual-editor's runtime span injection into option children, not from app code. Not a real bug.
delete_user cascades events but not preferences/notifications documents — minor data hygiene.
seed_data_creation: None beyond built-in seed users. Test-created data (TEST_* events/users) cleaned up in-line.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py runs against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Uses Bearer token from login response (cookies also set). Emergent visual-editor injects spans into <option> at runtime producing a benign React hydration warning — ignore unless real UI issues surface. Speech Recognition mic button cannot be exercised in headless; use voice-transcript-input textarea instead.
